# csi2_raw_unpack: generation prompt

## 1. Identity

- Module name: `csi2_raw_unpack`
- Library category: `video`
- Location: `ip/video/csi2_raw_unpack/`
- One-line purpose: CSI-2 RAW payload unpacker.
- Version: 1.0.0

## 2. Context

- Where it is used: `video_pipeline`, `video_processor`.
- Existing IP to reuse (do not duplicate): none; self-contained.

## 3. Parameters

| Name | Default | Meaning / legal range |
|---|---|---|
| `IN_BYTES` | `2` | bytes per input word (CSI-2 lanes) |
| `OUT_W` | `10` | output pixel width |

Reject illegal values at elaboration with `$error` inside a generate block.

## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 5. Interfaces

- **s_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream slave (input), tdata [IN_BYTES*8-1:0], tkeep, tlast, tuser: interface `axis_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).
- **m_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream master (output), tdata [OUT_W-1:0], tlast, tuser: interface `axis_if.master` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).

Bus ports follow the library's SystemVerilog interfaces, one definition file per type: AXI4-Stream `axis_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`, modports master / slave / monitor) and AXI4-Lite `axil_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`, modports master / slave). Icarus Verilog cannot drive members of interface arrays and Yosys reads interfaces only through sv2v, so keep discrete ports (<prefix>_tdata, <prefix>_awaddr, ...) and put the interface and modport in a comment line directly above each port group: `// s_axis: axis_if.slave (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 24`. Testbenches and Verilator flows may instantiate the interfaces directly.

| Port | Dir | Width | Group | Built when | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clk` | input | 1 | - | - | - |
| `rst_n` | input | 1 | - | - | - |
| `fmt_i` | input | [5:0] | - | - | CSI-2 data type (change between frames) |

Back-pressure on every stream: honour tready, never drop data unless section 6 says so; valid must not depend combinationally on ready.

AXI4-Lite / register map: as listed in the behaviour text in section 6. Out-of-range accesses return SLVERR (or DECERR where stated).

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
CSI-2 RAW payload unpacker. Version 1.0.0. Converts the
packed payload bytes of csi2_rx (IN_BYTES bytes per word, tkeep
contiguous from bit 0, tlast = end of line, tuser = start of frame)
into one pixel per clock in the AXI-Stream video format of this library
(tuser = SOF on the first pixel, tlast = EOL on the last pixel of a line).
Formats (fmt_i = CSI-2 data type):
  0x2A RAW8  - 1 byte  -> 1 pixel
  0x2B RAW10 - 5 bytes -> 4 pixels: bytes 0-3 hold bits [9:2] of pixels
               0-3, byte 4 holds bits [1:0] of pixel i in bits [2i+1:2i]
  0x2C RAW12 - 3 bytes -> 2 pixels: bytes 0-1 hold bits [11:4], byte 2
               holds bits [3:0] of pixel 0 in [3:0], pixel 1 in [7:4]
Pixels are aligned to OUT_W bits (shifted left when narrower, right when
wider). A line must hold whole groups (CSI-2 requires this). Unknown
formats are treated as RAW8.
Resync - grouping is checked against the line and frame markers: a group
that would run past the end of a line drops the bytes up to that end,
and one that would start before a start-of-frame byte drops the bytes
before it. Payload words lost upstream (e.g. a full clock-crossing FIFO)
therefore corrupt at most the line they belong to. Throughput - 1 pixel per clock; the input
is back-pressured while the byte buffer is full. Clock - clk only.
Reset - synchronous rst_n (active low). Latency - 2 clocks.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - csi2_raw_unpack (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] MIPI Alliance, "Specification for Camera Serial Interface 2 (CSI-2)" v1.3 (2014):
//   9.1-9.6 low level protocol (DI, WC, 6-bit header ECC, CRC-16 x^16+x^12+x^5+1 seed 0xFFFF),
//   11 data formats (RGB888 0x24 B,G,R; YUV422 8-bit 0x1E U,Y,V,Y; RAW8 0x2A, RAW10 0x2B, RAW12
//   0x2C); vendor summary AMD PG232 https://docs.amd.com/r/5.1-English/pg232-mipi-csi2-rx/MIPI-
//   CSI-2-RX-Controller
//   [2] Linux V4L2, "10-bit packed Bayer formats" (CSI-2 RAW10: four MSB bytes then one byte of
//   2-bit LSBs, pixel 0 in bits [1:0]), https://docs.kernel.org/5.3/media/uapi/v4l/pixfmt-
//   srggb10p.html
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   CSI-2 RAW8 (0x2A) one byte per pixel; RAW10 (0x2B) 4 pixels in 5 bytes, bytes 0-3 = bits
//   [9:2], byte 4 = bits [1:0] of pixels 0..3 in bits [1:0], [3:2], [5:4], [7:6]; RAW12 (0x2C)
//   2 pixels in 3 bytes, byte 2 = pixel 0 bits [3:0] in [3:0], pixel 1 in [7:4].
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches both packings exactly; line lengths in whole groups as CSI-2 requires.
// Result: in line with the reference; no TODO.
```


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: Last Yosys synth_xilinx (7-series) result: about 380 LUTs, 119 flip-flops. Stay within about this budget.

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking testbench for csi2_raw_unpack. Four instances
(IN_BYTES 1, 2, 4 with OUT_W 10, and IN_BYTES 2 with OUT_W 12) unpack
RAW8, RAW10 and RAW12 frames whose lines end in partial words, with
random input gaps and output back-pressure. Every pixel value (aligned
to OUT_W), tuser and tlast is checked. Resync: a frame that loses a
payload word in the middle of a line must be followed by a frame that
is unpacked exactly. Prints TEST PASSED on success.
The test tasks are in tests/csi2_raw_unpack_tests.sv (`included).
```

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh csi2_raw_unpack --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `csi2_raw_unpack_tb` | `csi2_raw_unpack_tb` | one test: Self-checking testbench for csi2_raw_unpack. |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C video/csi2_raw_unpack test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.
